title: Abolish the NICs upper earnings limit
headline: Abolish the NICs upper earnings limit: 8% all the way up. IFS, £14.1bn, static.
description: Employees pay 8% National Insurance on earnings up to £50,270 and 2% above it; the self-employed pay 6% and 2%. Abolishing the upper earnings and upper profits limits charges the main rate on every pound: the IFS Green Budget scores it at £14.1 billion a year by 2029-30, mostly from the highest-income tenth of households, and warns that behavioural responses would be likely to reduce that significantly. Held flat in cash. It is a six-point rise in the rate paid on earnings above £50,270 and, on the game’s reading, breaks the tax lock.

baselinePolicy.text: Employee NICs are 8% between the primary threshold and the upper earnings limit of £50,270 and 2% above it; Class 4 is 6% and 2%. The limits are frozen with the income tax thresholds.
alreadyIncludes: The freeze in the upper earnings limit to April 2031 with the income tax thresholds (Budget 2025 line 46).

terms.label: The IFS Green Budget’s static yield from abolishing the upper earnings limit and upper profits limit

source.quote: Abolish upper earnings limit and upper profits limit £14.1billion

rawSource.note: The IFS’s Table 9.3 figure for 2029-30, held flat in cash from the start year. Static, and the IFS says behaviour would cut it significantly.

caveats: Static. The IFS says "Behavioural responses would be likely to reduce this yield significantly": the marginal rate on earnings above £50,270 rises six points, and above £100,000 the combined rate already reaches 62%.
The 2% additional rate slider on this tab is a smaller version of the same thing; do not stack them.
A NICs rate rise for everyone earning over £50,270, which the game treats as breaking the manifesto lock.

considerations.text: The IFS’s £14.1 billion is a static figure and it says so: with a six-point rise in the marginal rate on high earnings, incorporation, pension contributions and reduced hours would take a significant share of the yield.

sources.quote: Behavioural responses would be likely to reduce this yield significantly, however.

considerations.text: Employees and the self-employed earning over £50,270; the IFS says the yield comes mostly from the highest-income tenth of households, and it is akin to a six-point rise in the higher and additional rates of income tax.

sources.quote: mostly from the highest-income tenth of households

considerations.text: The manifesto promises not to increase National Insurance. Charging 8% instead of 2% above £50,270 is a rise in the rate for everyone above it, so the game treats this switch as breaking the tax lock.

sources.quote: we will not increase National Insurance, the basic, higher, or additional rates of Income Tax, or VAT

interactions.text: Abolishing the upper earnings limit replaces the 2% additional rate altogether; raising that rate as well double counts.
With no upper limit, every point on the main rate applies to all earnings, so the two compound.
